dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product lets files be dropped on a whole working screen — a list of documents, a library of videos, a conversation — and not only on a bounded place inside a form. It shows the same answer wherever such a screen stands: while files are dragged over it, the whole screen is covered and says, in one message, that letting go here adds them.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a drop zone reads, all of it drawn only while files are dragged over it: the scrim over its content; the edge drawn inside its box (width, and color while it takes the drag and while it refuses it); the panel at the centre of the part of the zone that is in view (fill, elevation, corners, paddings, gap, widest width, and its least distance to the zone's edges); the glyph's size and its colors; the message's text style and color; and the timing of the overlay's fade.
rules: A drop zone draws nothing at rest and adds no hover, no press, no focus stop and no role: what it wraps is used as if it were not there. It answers a drag of files alone.
Dragging is never the only way to add a file: a page with a drop zone also offers a File picker or a File upload whose Button opens the platform's picker.
The overlay is one layer over the whole zone: scrim, edge and panel. It never takes a press or a scroll, so it never needs to be dismissed.
refusing is drawn only where the platform tells before the drop that nothing dragged can be taken; it is the drag's condition, not an error the product sets.
For a bounded place inside a form that is also pressed to open the picker, use the File picker's drop-area layout instead.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a drop overlay by hand.

color.$description: The dim over the zone's content while files are dragged over it, alpha included (the scrim role is the overlay as drawn): the content is still there, and not what is pointed at now.

width.$description: The edge drawn inside the zone's box while files are dragged over it: the heavier stroke, the mark of what is selected, because the whole zone is the place now chosen.

color.$description: That edge while the zone will take what is dragged over it.
The panel that holds the glyph and the message, over the scrim: a raised surface, so that the message is read on its own ground whatever content lies under the scrim.

elevation.$description: The panel's lift over the scrim.

shape.$description: Every corner of the panel: the step of a surface raised over the content, as a dialog's.

padding-block.$description: The room above the glyph and below the message.

padding-inline.$description: The room at the panel's start and end.

gap.$description: The space between the glyph and the message.

max-width.$description: The widest the panel draws; a longer message wraps. A narrower zone gives the panel its own width less panel.margin on each side.

margin.$description: The least distance between the panel and the zone's edges: the panel never touches the edge, and never leaves the zone.

size.$description: The glyph above the message: the largest step of the icon scale, as the File picker's drop area's.

color.$description: The glyph while the zone will take what is dragged over it: the color of its edge.

typescale.$description: The message: running text one step larger than the interface's, because it is read at a glance during a drag.

color.$description: The message on the panel: the surface's text color.

refusing.$description: The overlay while what is dragged over the zone cannot be taken. The scrim, the panel and the message's color stay as while it takes it.

color.$description: The edge while the zone will not take what is dragged over it: the error role, because letting go here fails.
The glyph, which becomes the icon set's block glyph, in the same role.

duration.$description: How long the overlay takes to fade in when a drag of files enters the zone, and to fade out when it leaves, ends or drops; and how long a change between taking and refusing takes.
